paper.title: The chemical basis of morphogenesis
paper.journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London B 237(641):37-72

headline: Turing 1952 diffusion-driven instability (Gierer-Meinhardt, grid-PDE): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; control CoV=0.0002 vs Turing CoV=1.060; k_meas=0.867 vs linear-theory q*=0.829

verdicts.gate: P1 diffusion-driven instability: control d=1 stays homogeneous (CoV<0.05) AND Turing d=1.5 d_c forms a finite-amplitude pattern (CoV>>0.05)
P2 wavelength matches linear dispersion: k_meas in the unstable band AND |k_meas - q*|/q* <= 0.35 (q* derived from the GM Jacobian)
P3 stationary non-oscillatory pattern: last-20% amplitude flat (< 5% relative change per 1000 steps) for every seed

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce Turing's diffusion-driven instability (homogeneous without differential diffusion, patterned with it, at the dispersion-relation wavelength) and would catch an artifact

citations: Turing, A.M. (1952). The chemical basis of morphogenesis. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London B 237(641):37-72. doi:10.1098/rstb.1952.0012.
Gierer, A. & Meinhardt, H. (1972). A theory of biological pattern formation. Kybernetik 12(1):30-39. doi:10.1007/BF00289234.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the spatial CoV, the dispersion-relation wavenumber, and amplitude stationarity
